cards.b: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

cards.f: Which test proves an object is a magnet?
cards.b: Repulsion with another magnet. Attraction could be to an unmagnetised magnetic material.
Soft iron is easily magnetised and demagnetised (temporary magnet, cores). Steel keeps its magnetism (permanent magnet).
Electromagnet is magnetic only while current flows and its strength can be changed; permanent magnet is always magnetic with fixed strength.
A region in which a magnetic pole experiences a force.

cards.f: Direction of a magnetic field line
cards.b: The direction of the force on a N pole: from N to S outside a magnet. Lines never cross; closest where field is strongest.
A magnetic material in a magnetic field becomes a magnet; the end nearest a N pole becomes a S pole, so it is attracted.

cards.f: Field around a straight current-carrying wire
cards.b: Concentric circles around the wire; direction by right-hand grip rule; stronger with larger current and closer to wire.
Strong and uniform (parallel, evenly spaced lines); outside it resembles a bar magnet's field.

cards.f: Ways to strengthen a solenoid's field
cards.b: Larger current, more turns, soft-iron core.
First finger = Field (N to S), seCond finger = Current (+ to −), thuMb = Motion (force).

cards.f: How to reverse the force on a current-carrying wire in a field
cards.b: Reverse the current or reverse the field (reversing both leaves the force unchanged).

cards.f: Why does a d.c. motor coil rotate?
cards.b: Current in the two sides is in opposite directions, so forces are opposite, producing a turning effect.
Reverses the current in the coil every half turn so the coil keeps turning the same way.

Increasing the number of turns on a motor coil ___ its turning effect.

short.q: Describe how to show that a force acts on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field.
short.model: Place a wire (or rod on rails) between the poles of a U-shaped magnet and connect it to a d.c. supply. When the current flows the wire moves; reversing the current or the field reverses the movement.
points: wire between magnet poles with d.c. supply
reversing current or field reverses force

short.q: State three ways of increasing the turning effect of a d.c. motor.
short.model: Increase the current, use a stronger magnetic field, increase the number of turns on the coil.

short.q: Explain the function of the brushes and split-ring commutator in a d.c. motor.
short.model: Brushes connect the rotating coil to the supply. The commutator reverses the current every half turn, so the forces keep the coil turning in the same direction.
points: brushes make contact with the supply
commutator reverses current each half turn

short.q: Explain why a soft-iron core is used in an electromagnet while a steel core is not.
short.model: Soft iron is easily magnetised and loses its magnetism when the current is switched off. Steel would stay magnetised.

short.q: A magnet attracts a nail. Explain why this does not prove the nail is a magnet, and how to test it.
short.model: The nail may be an unmagnetised piece of iron or steel, which is attracted by induced magnetism. Only repulsion of a magnet's pole proves it is a magnet.
points: attraction also happens with unmagnetised magnetic material
